messages:
AcmeInc - ops: Hey @Aisha — our Embeddings Usage chart in Console shows ~3.2M units for today but our application logs show ~1.1M vectors generated. Billing alert fired. dashboard: https://console.redwood.example.com/orgs/acmeinc/usage :eyes:
Aisha (support): Thanks — can you share a couple of request IDs and the approximate timestamps? Also: are you batching on the client side?
AcmeInc - ops: Yes we batch 10 per request, X-Request-ID on one sample: req-20260315-abc123 at 2026-03-15T14:12:22Z. Another: req-20260315-def456 at 2026-03-15T14:15:09Z. We also enable prefix caching (we send repeated similar input).
Aisha (support): Copying in eng-metrics: @Diego can you triage? It smells like a mismatch between vectors vs tokens counting or duplicate ingestion from a replay/backfill.
Diego (eng-metrics): looking. Quick hypothesis: we recently changed the telemetry pipeline to emit both per-vector counts (embeddings.vectors_count) and a generic embeddings.units gauge, and two different collectors may be incrementing the same billing counter. Also backfill job ran last night. Can you paste a raw request payload or the API call you used?
AcmeInc - ops: here's a curl we used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'X-Request-ID: req-20260315-abc123' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["a","b",...10 items...]}'```
AcmeInc - ops: note: client library does automatic retry on 5xx with idempotency disabled (old client).
Diego (eng-metrics): important — if retry+no-idempotency and both collectors consume the request, we can double count. Running quick query against metrics store to check duplicates by request id: ```sql
-- clickhouse example
SELECT request_id, metric_name, count() as cnt
FROM metrics.events
WHERE metric_name IN ('embeddings.vectors_count','embeddings.units')
  AND timestamp >= '2026-03-15 00:00:00'
  AND timestamp <= '2026-03-15 23:59:59'
GROUP BY request_id, metric_name
HAVING cnt > 1
LIMIT 50;
```
Diego (eng-metrics): also check whether the backfill job emitted events without the request_id, causing aggregation to fall back to a coarse key and double-sum across windows.
Aisha (support): I ran the above query for your two sample request_ids — I see req-20260315-abc123 appears twice for embeddings.units and once for embeddings.vectors_count.
Sam (prod): adding context — we rolled out metrics-pipeline v2 yesterday at 02:00 UTC which introduced the new "units" metric and a streaming+batch merge step. Backfill started 03:30 UTC to populate historical vectors_count -> units mapping. The backfill had a bug that replayed some streaming events.
MetricsBot: automated: backfill-job/embeddings-run finished: status=COMPLETED, rows_processed=12,340,567, started=2026-03-15T03:30:12Z, finished=2026-03-15T05:14:02Z
Diego (eng-metrics): OK that aligns. Likely root cause = streaming events + backfill replayed same logical requests into billing aggregator without de-dup key. Immediate mitigations: 1) stop the backfill replay (if still running), 2) enable request_id dedupe in aggregator, 3) run a correction job to subtract duplicates for affected window.
Aisha (support): Will escalate to priority-1 billing incident if customer is billed incorrectly. @Sam can you pause backfill and enable dedupe toggle?
Sam (prod): Pausing backfill now. Toggle set to dedupe=true for billing-aggregator (flag: billing.dedupe_requests=true). Patch deployed to aggregator to prefer request_id as primary key.
Diego (eng-metrics): next steps for investigation: run this to get total suspected duplicate units per org: ```sql
SELECT org_id, sum((cnt - 1) * units) as suspected_overcount
FROM (
  SELECT org_id, request_id, anyLast(units) as units, count() as cnt
  FROM metrics.events
  WHERE metric_name = 'embeddings.units'
    AND timestamp >= '2026-03-15'
  GROUP BY org_id, request_id
) WHERE cnt > 1
GROUP BY org_id
ORDER BY suspected_overcount DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
Aisha (support): I've run that for AcmeInc — suspected_overcount = 2,141,200 units for 2026-03-15 to date. Flagging billing team.
AcmeInc - ops: Wow — thanks. Is there a repro so we can adjust client side too?
Diego (eng-metrics): repro steps (short): 1) send a batched embedding request with X-Request-ID header 2) simulate streaming consumer + run backfill replay for same timestamp range 3) observe duplicate increments in metrics.events for that request_id. Example test script: ```python
# pseudocode
r = post('/v1/embeddings', json={"input":[...10 items...]}, headers={'X-Request-ID': 'dup-test-1'})
# on ingest: emit metric embeddings.units += 10
# run replay job that also emits embeddings.units for same request_id
# assert count(metrics where request_id='dup-test-1' and metric='embeddings.units') == 1
```
Sam (prod): we'll create a hotfix to ignore events from backfill that contain request_id when aggregator dedupe is on. Also preparing correction plan to credit affected customers.
Aisha (support): assigning to eng-metrics for root cause + correction. I set incident severity=high and cc billing. @Diego please post final postmortem when done. :thumbsup:
AcmeInc - ops: Thanks for the quick triage. We'll hold on billing dispute until you confirm correction plan.
Diego (eng-metrics): noted. I'll follow up with exact windows and a CSV of request_ids for audit. ETA 4 hours.
